classification.class: stack-buffer-underflow read from an off-by-one packed argument lookup

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42483087 (fmt): Stack-buffer-underflow READ 16 found by fuzz target fuzzer_named_arg [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42483087
bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta issue description / exact staged vulnerable source from the ARVO workspace container / staged patch.diff / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / staged reproduction_report.json / staged poc bytes
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged vulnerable source that reproduced the crash is the ARVO workspace checkout `8a4630686e2dd24900897298c4ae1362de749ed8`, not metadata vulnerable commit `8a11148f9918f266b1e0155d31b3ea783b07d6a5`. In that staged tree, the 22-byte witness `11 ff ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 7b 31 32 7d` makes `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` choose the `char` instantiation with `argsize = 1`. `invoke_fmt<char>` copies the first post-control byte into `item1`, skips the fixed 16-byte value slot, copies the next byte into separately allocated argument name `" "`, and copies the remaining four bytes into separately allocated format string `{12}`. `fmt::format_to` then builds a one-argument packed `format_arg_store`: `desc` encodes the underlying `char_type` for slot 0 and also sets `has_named_args_bit`, while `data_.args()` exposes only the single actual value slot after the reserved named-argument-metadata entry. When the format parser sees `{12}`, `parse_arg_id` converts the attacker-controlled digits to `index = 12` and passes that id into `basic_format_args::do_get`. The vulnerable packed-path guard `if (index > internal::max_packed_args)` treats `index == 12` as in range even though packed slots exist only for indices 0 through 11. `type(12)` therefore reads the high descriptor bits, interprets `has_named_args_bit` as `internal::type::long_long_type`, skips the `none_type` return, and `val = values_[12]` copies a 16-byte `internal::value` from outside the one-element packed array. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting `stack-buffer-underflow READ of size 16` in `basic_format_args::do_get`; the staged patch fixes the bug by changing the guard to `>=`.

source.description: First non-entry-point project statement on the crashing path that consumes attacker-controlled bytes and materializes the eventual named-argument value.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` is exactly 22 bytes: `11 ff ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 7b 31 32 7d`. Byte 0 `0x11` makes `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` set `first = 1` and `second = 1`, selecting `invoke_fmt<char>(Data + 1, Size - 1, 1)`. In that call `assignFromBuf<char>(Data)` consumes byte 1 as `item1`; `invoke_fmt` then advances by `fmt_fuzzer::Nfixed == 16`, so byte 17 becomes the one-byte argument name `" "` and bytes 18-21 become format string `{12}`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant attacker-controlled value is the manual replacement-field index `12`. This numeric branch materializes that integer from the copied format string `{12}` and forwards it into packed argument lookup.

sink.description: ASan sink. The packed lookup copies `values_[index]` into `arg.value_` after the nonexistent packed slot 12 has been treated as present.
sink.note: With the staged witness, `values_` still points to the one-element packed array created for the single named argument, but `index` is 12. AddressSanitizer reports this copy as `stack-buffer-underflow READ of size 16` with runtime top frame `__asan_memcpy` and project frames `basic_format_args::do_get -> basic_format_args::get`.

root_cause.description: Off-by-one bounds check in packed argument lookup: `index == internal::max_packed_args` is incorrectly treated as in range.
root_cause.note: In the staged source `internal::max_packed_args` is 12, but packed argument slots exist only for indices 0 through 11. The staged patch fixes this exact line by changing `>` to `>=`, which rejects the witnessed `index == 12` before `type(12)` or `values_[12]` execute.

packed_lookup_selected.code: static const bool is_packed = num_args <= internal::max_packed_args;
packed_lookup_selected.description: The call supplies exactly one argument, so `is_packed` is true and `basic_format_args::do_get` later executes the packed lookup path that contains the off-by-one guard.

parser_admitted.description: The copied format string `{12}` is syntactically valid as a manual-index replacement field, so parsing reaches numeric argument lookup instead of rejecting the field.

evidence_limitations: The exact reproducing ARVO workspace checkout is `8a4630686e2dd24900897298c4ae1362de749ed8`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `8a11148f9918f266b1e0155d31b3ea783b07d6a5`. All line numbers and code quotes below are grounded in that staged source because it is the tree that actually reproduced and matches the saved patch context.

The saved ASan frame for `basic_format_args::do_get` does not carry an exact source line, so `include/fmt/core.h:1595` is identified from the staged vulnerable source as the only 16-byte packed-value copy in `do_get` that remains after the admitted `index == 12` path.

coarse_trace.summary: The helper consumes one byte as `item1`, skips the fixed 16-byte slot, admits `argsize == 1` against the remaining `Size == 5`, then copies the one-byte name and format string `{12}`.
Formatting one `named_arg` builds a packed descriptor with `has_named_args_bit` set and a `values_` view that exposes only one actual packed value slot.
Parsing `{12}` converts the attacker-controlled digits into integer lookup id 12.
The packed lookup admits `index == 12`, misreads `has_named_args_bit` as a real type, and then copies `values_[12]`, matching the saved stack-buffer-underflow.

fine_trace.note: Source. After the control byte `0x11` selects `invoke_fmt<char>` with `argsize == 1`, this statement copies the first remaining input byte into `item1`. The helper later skips the full 16-byte fixed slot, so this byte becomes the only actual packed argument value on the crashing path.

After `item1` is materialized, the helper skips the fixed 16-byte value slot. From the Stage 01 witness this rewrites the live window to `Data` at byte 17 with `Size == 5`; because `argsize == 1`, the guard is false and execution continues into the named-argument copy.
Using the post-`Nfixed` window from step 2, `memcpy` copies the single live byte `0x20` into a separate buffer and exposes it as the one-character argument name `" "`.

After the one-byte name is consumed, the helper advances past it. This moves `Data` from witness byte 17 to byte 18 and shrinks `Size` from 5 to 4, leaving exactly the bytes `7b 31 32 7d` for the format string.
Using the post-name window from step 4, the remaining four bytes `7b 31 32 7d` are copied into a second tight allocation and exposed as `fmtstring == "{12}"`.

This call site supplies exactly one `fmt::arg(argname, item1)`, so `num_args == 1`, `num_named_args == 1`, and `is_packed` is true. `desc` therefore combines the packed type for the underlying `char` value with `has_named_args_bit`. In the packed constructor, `internal::make_arg<true, Context>` reaches `arg_mapper::map(const named_arg<T, char_type>&)` and stores `item1`'s underlying `char_type` value in `data_`, while `arg_data` keeps the separate named-argument metadata in its extra `args_[0]` slot and `args()` later skips that slot.

The `basic_format_args` view copies `store.desc` into `desc_` and sets `values_` to `store.data_.args()`. Because `args()` returns `args_ + 1`, `values_` now points at the single actual packed value slot and not at the reserved named-argument metadata entry.
Parsing the replacement field inside `fmtstring` takes the numeric-id branch, converts the digits `12` to integer `index = 12`, and passes that id to the handler.

Root cause. In packed mode `internal::max_packed_args` is 12, but real packed argument slots exist only for indices 0 through 11. The attacker-controlled `index == 12` therefore takes the false branch and is treated as valid.

fine_trace.code:
arg.type_ = type(index);
if (arg.type_ == internal::type::none_type) return arg;
fine_trace.note: With `index == 12`, `type(index)` shifts `desc_` right by 60 bits. The only live bits there come from `has_named_args_bit` (`1ULL << 62`), so `(desc_ >> 60) & 0x1f` becomes `4` (`internal::type::long_long_type`) instead of `none_type`. The nonexistent slot is therefore misclassified as present and the early return is skipped.

Sink. `values_` still points to the one-element packed array from step 7, but the admitted `index == 12` makes this assignment copy one whole `internal::value<Context>` from `values_[12]` into `arg.value_`. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports that copy as `stack-buffer-underflow READ of size 16` with runtime top frame `__asan_memcpy` and project frames `basic_format_args::do_get -> basic_format_args::get`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, patch.diff, exact staged vulnerable source from the ARVO workspace container, and the saved witness bytes; runtime disambiguation was disabled in run_flags.json

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch changes the exact guard in `basic_format_args::do_get` from `>` to `>=`, which blocks the witnessed `index == 12` path before `type(12)` or `values_[12]` execute.

poc.trigger: The saved Stage 01 command `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42483087 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` runs `fuzzer_named_arg` on this exact file and reproduces `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-underflow READ of size 16` in `basic_format_args::do_get` with runtime top frame `__asan_memcpy`.

format.name: raw named-argument fuzzer input
format.contract: Exactly the 22-byte witness stored in `poc`: `11 ff ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 7b 31 32 7d`. Byte 0 `0x11` selects the `char` instantiation and `argsize = 1`; `invoke_fmt<char>` always skips a 16-byte value slot, so the next byte becomes a one-character argument name `" "` and the remaining four bytes are format string `{12}`. The verified trigger is limited to this witnessed configuration of one `named_arg` plus replacement field `12`, which reaches packed lookup with `index == internal::max_packed_args == 12`; the staged artifacts do not justify a broader class of indices, argument counts, or format layouts.
